data.narrative:
Redwood Materials, a Series E climate and energy company founded by J.B. Straubel, is evaluated against a comparable universe of 9 peers (1 public, 8 private), including QuantumScape, KoBold Metals, Electric Hydrogen, Enovix, and Amogy. The company has raised $2.125B to date and carries a current post-money valuation of $6.0B.

The valuation analysis applies a stage-progression methodology, the only triangulation approach with sufficient data support. This method applies a 1.4x step-up multiplier typical of Series E to later-stage progression to the company's $6.0B last post-money valuation, yielding an implied valuation of $8.4B. A peer-median approach could not be applied due to insufficient narrow-filtered comparables in the Climate & Energy sector; while 7 same-sector peers exist, none of the tighter stage and valuation-tier filters produced three or more datapoints necessary for reliable median estimation.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $7.1B to $9.7B, with a central estimate of $8.4B. Key uncertainties stem from the limited applicability of peer-median methods and the reliance on a single forward-step multiplier. The narrowness of the comparable set—particularly at equivalent stage and scale—limits confidence in downside and upside scenarios absent additional methodological inputs.
